evidence.note: When early yeast runs plateaued the agent changed meaningful levers: made temperatures configurable to switch between hill-climbing and SA, then added sideways moves to traverse plateaus — targeted mechanism changes, then re-measured.

For DM-HS the agent cycled through distinct initialization strategies (topological signatures, seed-and-extend, wiring-aware percolation) and then made a major algorithm change (topologically-guided local move generator) rather than re-running the same greedy match.

Genuine bottleneck diagnosis: reasoned from the S3 formula that hub-matching bias inflates E2_aligned in the denominator, so switched to random-start SA to find sparser mappings — hypothesis-driven, metric-aware course correction (anchor-8 behavior).

Reheating rounds 1-4 largely repeat the same intervention with only slightly-tuned temperatures, all converging ~0.311-0.313 without a new hypothesis for the 0.32 barrier — a trivial-tweak pattern that keeps this below a clean 10.
Preserved best-known solutions (risk-free hill climbing, evaluating multiple candidate files to select the best) and decisively killed lingering/inferior runs, deploying the best alignment.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5 (changing meaningful levers and re-measuring) and hits anchor 8: it diagnoses WHY targets are missed — notably the E2_aligned/hub-bias reasoning at step 172 — then makes targeted changes (random init, annealing schedules, guided move generator, sideways moves) and re-measures, while preserving best solutions and abandoning dead ends. It falls short of a clean 10 because the late-stage DM-HS reheating rounds repeat essentially the same lever with only trivial temperature tweaks and no fresh hypothesis about the persistent 0.32 plateau.
